entry: Fluid with [[Viscosity|viscosity]] dependent on stress. Non-Newtonian fluids do not follow Newton's law of viscosity, so their viscosity can change when force is applied. [[Ketchup]] becomes runnier when shaken, and many salt solutions, molten polymers, [[Paint]], [[Blood]] and melted butter are non-Newtonian. A common demonstration is Oobleck, a mixture of corn or potato starch and water, which shows shear thickening: it grows more viscous when disturbed and briefly becomes a near-solid mass under sudden impact. Because viscosity alone cannot fully describe these fluids, they are studied with other rheological properties measured by rheometers.

Gender identities outside the male/female gender binary. Non-binary identities, also written nonbinary or genderqueer, often fall under the [[Transgender|transgender]] umbrella, since non-binary people typically identify with a gender different from their sex assigned at birth. Some identify as an intermediate or third gender, with more than one gender or none. Gender identity is separate from sexual orientation. Some receive gender-affirming care to reduce distress from gender dysphoria. In the early 2010s non-binary surpassed genderqueer as the most-used umbrella term, though some critics say it reinforces the concept of a binary.

Nongovernmental entity, usually nonprofit, abbreviated NGO. An NGO may be nonprofit or for-profit and may receive all or most of its funding from [[Government|government]] sources, but it operates independently of government control. The term was introduced in Article 71 of the [[United Nations]] Charter in 1945. The UN Department of Global Communications defines an NGO as "a not-for-profit, voluntary citizen's group that is organized on a local, national or international level to address issues in support of the public good." The term is used inconsistently and sometimes as a synonym for [[Civil society|civil society organization]] (CSO). NGOs are classified by orientation, such as [[Human rights|human rights]], consumer protection, [[Environmentalism|environmentalism]] or [[Health|health]], and by level of operation: local, regional, national or international. Russia had about 277,000 NGOs in 2008. The United States has approximately 1.5 million, one for every 227 people.

Sexual activity that usually excludes penetration, also called outercourse. It generally excludes the penetrative aspects of vaginal, anal or [[Oral sex|oral sex]], but includes frottage, manual sex, mutual masturbation, kissing and hugging. Outercourse may include penetrative aspects, such as from [[Fingering (sexual act)|fingering]] or oral sex. People engage in it as [[Foreplay|foreplay]], as a preferred act, or to preserve [[Virginity|virginity]]. Although [[Herpes|herpes]], HPV and pubic lice can be transmitted through non-penetrative genital contact, it may be used as safer sex because body fluids, the main source of [[Sexually transmitted infection|sexually transmitted infection]] transmission, are less likely to be exchanged.

Process of solving optimization problems that are not linear. Nonlinear programming (NLP), also called nonlinear optimization, is the sub-field of [[Mathematical optimization|mathematical optimization]] dealing with problems in which some constraints are not linear equalities or the objective function is not linear. An optimization problem seeks the extrema (maxima, minima or stationary points) of an objective function over a set of unknown real variables, subject to equalities and [[Inequality (mathematics)|inequalities]], called constraints. A problem is feasible if at least one set of values satisfies all constraints; it is infeasible if no solution exists, because the feasible set is the [[Empty set|empty set]]. If the objective is concave (maximized) or convex (minimized) over a convex constraint set, general convex optimization methods can be used. Quadratic objectives with linear constraints call for quadratic programming techniques. The Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions give necessary conditions for optimality under differentiability and constraint qualifications.

[[Chemical element]] that mostly lacks distinctive metallic properties. Nonmetals range from colorless gases such as [[Hydrogen|hydrogen]] to lustrous crystalline solids such as [[Iodine|iodine]]. They are usually less dense than metals and are often poor conductors of heat and electricity. Chemically they have moderate to very high [[Electronegativity|electronegativity]], and their oxides tend to be [[Acid|acidic]]. Seventeen elements are widely recognized as nonmetals, and some or all of six borderline elements, called [[Metalloid|metalloids]], are sometimes counted as nonmetals too. Hydrogen and helium make up about 98% of the mass of ordinary matter in the observable universe.

Organization operated for collective, public or social benefit rather than profit. A nonprofit organization (NPO), also called a non-business entity or nonprofit institution, is a non-governmental entity subject to a non-distribution constraint: any revenue exceeding expenses must be used to further its purpose. Depending on local law, nonprofits may include charities, political organizations, schools, hospitals, [[Business|business associations]], churches, foundations, social clubs and cooperatives. In some countries they may obtain tax-exempt status and receive tax-deductible contributions, although a nonprofit need not be tax-exempt. They are accountable to donors, founders, volunteers, program recipients and the public. The number of nonprofits rose significantly between 2000 and 2023, to approximately 1.5 million registered organizations in the [[United States|United States]] alone. In the United States, state law grants nonprofit status, while the federal government grants tax-exempt designations such as IRC 501(c).

Form of [[Christianity|Christianity]] that rejects the [[Trinity|doctrine of the Trinity]]. The Trinity is the belief that God is three distinct persons who are coeternal, coequal and indivisibly united in one being or essence. Nontrinitarian denominations comprise about 3% of modern Christians. The largest are the Oneness Pentecostal movement, [[The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints|The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints]] and [[Jehovah's Witnesses|Jehovah's Witnesses]]. Some groups that emerged during the [[Reformation|Protestant Reformation]] were known as antitrinitarian. Churches that consider ecumenical councils final hold that trinitarianism was declared Christian doctrine at the First Council of Nicaea (325), which declared the full divinity of the Son, and the First Council of Constantinople (381), which declared the divinity of the Holy Spirit. Earlier nontrinitarian views, such as adoptionism and monarchianism, predated the codification of the Trinity doctrine at the councils of Nicaea, Constantinople and Ephesus. Nontrinitarianism was renewed in the [[Unitarianism|Unitarian]] movement and in some groups of the Second Great Awakening.

Interpersonal communication through wordless, mostly visual cues. Nonverbal communication transmits messages through eye contact (oculesics), [[Body language|body language]] (kinesics), social distance (proxemics), touch (haptics), voice (prosody and paralanguage), physical appearance and use of objects. The study of the subject began in 1872 with *The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals* by [[Charles Darwin|Charles Darwin]]. Encoding is the expression of emotions in ways a receiver can accurately interpret; decoding, called nonverbal sensitivity, is the accurate interpretation of those signals. For most communication, such as giving directions or teaching math, verbal information carries most of the meaning, though scholars argue that nonverbal communication can convey more meaning than words. Research by Albert Mehrabian in the 1960s led to the 7-38-55 rule: 7% words, 38% tone of voice and 55% facial expressions. The rule applies only in specific situations, such as when words contradict tone and expression.

Staple food made from unleavened dough, usually rolled flat and cut into long strips. Noodles are usually cooked in boiling water, sometimes with oil or salt, but may also be steamed, pan-fried, deep-fried or baked. The most common noodles derive from [[Chinese cuisine|Chinese cuisine]] or [[Italian cuisine|Italian cuisine]]; Italian noodles are generally called [[Pasta|pasta]]. In Chinese cuisine, miàn denotes noodles made from wheat or other grain dough, while fěn noodles, such as rice noodles, are made from starch slurry. The oldest physical evidence, an earthenware bowl with noodles at the Lajia archaeological site in China, dates to about 4,000 years ago, though some researchers doubt the noodles were made from millet. The earliest written record is in a book from the [[Han dynasty|Eastern Han period]] (25–220 CE). Noodles spread from China along the [[Silk Road|Silk Road]] to [[Central Asia|Central Asia]] and reached Persia by around the fourth century. Arab influence carried them to [[Sicily|Sicily]] and Spain, and they reached mainland Italy after the tenth century.

American writer, playwright, journalist and filmmaker, known for writing and directing romantic comedies. Her screenplays include *Silkwood* (1983), *Heartburn* (1986) and *When Harry Met Sally...* (1989), which earned a BAFTA Award for Best Original Screenplay. Her directed films include *Sleepless in Seattle* (1993), *You've Got Mail* (1998) and *Julie & Julia* (2009). She received nominations for three Academy Awards, a Tony Award and a Golden Globe Award. Her last play, *Lucky Guy* (2013), earned a posthumous Tony nomination for Best Play.

Geographical and cultural region in Northern Europe and North America. It includes the sovereign states of [[Denmark|Denmark]], Finland, [[Iceland|Iceland]], Norway and Sweden, the autonomous territories of the Faroe Islands and [[Greenland|Greenland]], and the autonomous region of [[Åland|Åland]]. Their social model combines a mixed market economy with strong labor unions and a universalist welfare sector financed by high taxes. The combined area is 3,425,804 sq km (1,322,710 sq mi), about half of it uninhabitable ice caps and glaciers, mainly in Greenland. In September 2021 the region had over 27 million people. In English, [[Scandinavia|Scandinavia]] is sometimes used as a synonym, but more properly refers to Denmark, Norway and Sweden.

External territory of [[Australia|Australia]] in the Pacific Ocean, between [[New Zealand|New Zealand]] and [[New Caledonia|New Caledonia]]. It had 2,188 inhabitants at the 2021 census, on about 35 sq km. East Polynesians settled it in the 13th or 14th century, but had left before Great Britain colonized it in 1788. It served as a convict penal settlement from 1788 until 1855, except for an 11-year hiatus between 1814 and 1825. Descendants of the Bounty mutineers were relocated from Pitcairn Island in 1856. The island was transferred from the United Kingdom to Australia in 1914. The native Norfolk Island pine is pictured on its flag.

Ceremonial county in the East of England, bordering Lincolnshire, Cambridgeshire, Suffolk and the North Sea. Predominantly rural, it had an estimated population of 940,359 in 2024, on 5,370 sq km (2,074 sq mi). The Iceni, led by [[Boudica|Boudica]], revolted against the Roman invasion in AD 60. During the later [[Middle Ages|Middle Ages]] the county was prosperous through the wool trade, which allowed the construction of many large churches. It was not heavily industrialized during the [[Industrial Revolution|Industrial Revolution]], and its economy is largely based on [[Agriculture|agriculture]] and tourism.

Industrial closed city in Krasnoyarsk Krai, Russia. Located south of the western Taymyr Peninsula, about 300 km north of the [[Arctic Circle|Arctic Circle]], it had a permanent population of 176,735 in 2024. It is the world's northernmost city with more than 50,000 inhabitants. Norilsk sits atop some of the largest [[Nickel|nickel]] deposits on Earth, and [[Mining|mining]] and [[Smelting|smelting]] are its major industries. Large-scale mining began after the Soviet Council of People's Commissars approved the Norilsk Plant in 1935. Norilsk and Yakutsk are the only large cities in the continuous [[Permafrost|permafrost]] zone.

Canadian stand-up comedian, actor and writer. He joined [[Saturday Night Live|Saturday Night Live]] as a writer and cast member in 1993 and anchored its Weekend Update segment for three and a half seasons. He was removed as host in 1998, allegedly for relentlessly mocking O. J. Simpson during his murder trial. His films include *Billy Madison* (1995) and *Dirty Work* (1998). He headlined the sitcom *The Norm Show* (1999–2001) and provided voice roles for [[Family Guy|Family Guy]]. He hosted talk shows including *Norm Macdonald Has a Show*, a Netflix series. He died of leukemia, a condition he had not publicly disclosed.

Function on a real or complex [[Vector space|vector space]] that generalizes length. A norm commutes with scaling, obeys a form of the triangle inequality and is zero only at the origin. The Euclidean norm, or 2-norm, is defined as the square root of the inner product of a vector with itself, and gives the magnitude of a vector in [[Euclidean space|Euclidean space]]. A seminorm may be zero for vectors other than the origin. The norm of a vector z is usually written as double vertical lines, a notation proposed by [[Stefan Banach|Stefan Banach]] in his doctoral thesis from 1920.

Continuous [[Probability distribution|probability distribution]] for a real-valued [[Random variable|random variable]]. Also called the Gaussian distribution, it is informally known as the bell curve, although many other distributions are bell-shaped. Its parameter μ is the mean, which is also the median and [[Mode (statistics)|mode]], and its parameter σ² is the [[Variance|variance]]; the positive value σ is the [[Standard deviation|standard deviation]]. Normal distributions are important in statistics and are often used to represent variables whose distributions are not known. Their importance is partly due to the [[Central limit theorem|central limit theorem]], which states that the average of many independent samples of a random variable with finite mean and variance converges to a normal distribution. Physical quantities that are the sum of many independent processes, such as measurement errors, are therefore often nearly normal. Any linear combination of independent normal deviates is itself normal. The standard normal distribution has mean 0 and variance 1.

American agronomist and plant pathologist who received the Nobel Peace Prize. Borlaug led initiatives that increased agricultural production in what became known as the [[Green Revolution|Green Revolution]]. He received a B.S. in forestry in 1937 and a PhD in plant pathology and genetics from the University of Minnesota in 1942. In [[Mexico|Mexico]] he developed semi-dwarf, high-yield, disease-resistant [[Wheat|wheat]] varieties, and he led their introduction to Mexico, [[Pakistan|Pakistan]] and [[India|India]]. Mexico became a net exporter of wheat by 1963, and between 1965 and 1970 wheat yields nearly doubled in Pakistan and India. He is credited with saving over a billion people from starvation, a figure traced to Gregg Easterbrook's 1997 article. He was awarded the 1970 Nobel Peace Prize for his contributions to world peace through increasing food supply, and is one of only seven people to have received the Nobel Peace Prize, the Presidential Medal of Freedom and the Congressional Gold Medal.

11th-century invasion of England by William, Duke of Normandy, later [[William the Conqueror|William the Conqueror]]. The army included thousands of Norman, French, Flemish and Breton troops. William's claim derived from his relationship with the childless Anglo-Saxon king [[Edward the Confessor|Edward the Confessor]]. After Edward's death in January 1066, Harold Godwinson became king, and Harald Hardrada was defeated at the [[Battle of Stamford Bridge|Battle of Stamford Bridge]] on 25 September. William landed at Pevensey on 28 September. Harold was killed at the [[Battle of Hastings|Battle of Hastings]] on 14 October, and William became king. William was not secure until after 1072. He confiscated the lands of the resisting English elite, granted lands to his followers and built castles. The [[Domesday Book|Domesday Book]] was completed by 1086. The conquest introduced a dialect of French as the language of the elites.

American [[Painting|painter]] and [[Illustration|illustrator]], best known for his covers for *The Saturday Evening Post*. Over nearly five decades he produced cover illustrations of everyday American life for the magazine. His works include the *Willie Gillis* series, *Rosie the Riveter*, the *Four Freedoms* series and *The Problem We All Live With*. He had a 64-year relationship with the Boy Scouts of America, producing covers for *Boys' Life*, and illustrated more than 40 books. He produced more than 4,000 original works and painted portraits of presidents Eisenhower, Kennedy, Johnson and Nixon, as well as [[Judy Garland|Judy Garland]]. Modern critics often find his work overly sweet. *The Problem We All Live With* (1964) depicts Ruby Bridges walking to school past a wall defaced with racist graffiti. The painting was displayed in the [[White House|White House]] when Bridges met [[Barack Obama|President Barack Obama]] in 2011.

Geographical and cultural region in northwestern Europe, roughly coextensive with the historical Duchy of Normandy. Mainland Normandy is part of France; insular Normandy is mostly the British [[Channel Islands|Channel Islands]]. It covers 30,627 sq km (11,825 sq mi), with a population of 3,499,280 in 2017. Its name comes from Viking settlement starting in the 9th century, confirmed by a treaty in the 10th century between King [[Charles III|Charles III]] of France and the Viking jarl Rollo. For almost 150 years after the [[Norman Conquest|Norman conquest]] of England in 1066, Normandy and England shared a ruler.

Allied landing operation of [[World War II|World War II]], commonly called D-Day. Codenamed Operation Neptune, the landings on 6 June 1944 formed part of Operation Overlord and were the largest seaborne invasion in history. The operation began the liberation of France and Western Europe. [[Adolf Hitler|Hitler]] placed [[Erwin Rommel|Erwin Rommel]] in command of German forces along the Atlantic Wall, and [[Dwight D. Eisenhower|Dwight D. Eisenhower]] commanded Allied forces. Following an airborne assault, landings occurred at five sectors along the coast of [[Normandy|Normandy]]. Allied casualties were at least 10,000, including 4,414 confirmed dead. German casualties have been estimated at 4,000 to 9,000 men.

Medieval population formed in the Duchy of [[Normandy|Normandy]] from Norse settlers and local West Franks. Norse Viking raids on the French coast led to settlement, and Rollo swore fealty to King Charles III of West Francia after the siege of Chartres in 911, forming the County of Rouen. The settlers adopted the language, religion and social customs of the West Franks, but retained mercenary tendencies and a fervor for adventure. Between 1066 and 1204 most kings of England were also dukes of Normandy, and the [[Norman Conquest|Norman conquest]] of England began at the [[Battle of Hastings|Battle of Hastings]]. Norman adventurers played a role in founding the [[Kingdom of Sicily|Kingdom of Sicily]], and their prince Bohemond I founded the [[Antioch|Principality of Antioch]]. Norman forces contributed to the [[Reconquista|Reconquista]]. Their legacy persists in regional languages and dialects of France, England, Spain, Quebec and Sicily.

Virus that is the most common cause of [[Gastroenteritis|gastroenteritis]], also known as Norwalk virus. Infection, sometimes called the winter vomiting disease or stomach flu, causes non-bloody [[Diarrhea|diarrhea]], vomiting and stomach pain, usually within 24 hours of exposure. Recovery typically takes one to three days, though dehydration can be a complication. It spreads mainly by the fecal-oral route. Norovirus causes about 685 million cases and 200,000 deaths globally each year, including about 50,000 deaths among children under five in the developing world. In the United States it causes about half of all foodborne disease outbreaks. There is no [[Vaccine|vaccine]] or specific treatment.
